title: Type Checking
summary: Luau's optional static type system: annotate variables, parameters, and returns (`local x: number`) and the analyzer catches mismatches before you run. The backbone of large Roblox codebases.

syntax: --!strict            -- mode comment at top of file

local function add(a: number, b: number): number
    return a + b
end
type PlayerData = { coins: number, level: number }

details.heading: Analysis modes
details.body: Per-script header comments: `--!strict` (full inference, errors on mismatch), `--!nonstrict`/`--!native` variants. Roblox Studio's Script Analysis shows the diagnostics; Luau-LSP in external editors powers autocomplete and inline errors.

details.heading: Core syntax
details.body: Annotations after `:` on locals, function params/returns, and table fields. `type Name = ...` declares aliases; `export type` makes them importable via `import type`. Built-ins: `number`, `string`, `boolean`, `nil`, `any`, `unknown`, `never`, unions `A | B`, intersections `A & B`, optional `T?`, arrays `{T}`, maps `{ [K]: V }`, functions `(number) -> string`.

details.heading: Casts and assertions
details.body: `x :: T` asserts a type (unchecked at runtime — the analyzer trusts you).

explanation.whatItIs: A spell-checker for your code's assumptions. You state what kind of value each thing should be; Luau's analyzer checks every use without running the game.
explanation.whyItExists: As projects grow, 'wait, was this a Player or a Character?' bugs multiply. Types push those errors left — into the editor, before play-testing.
whenToUse: New code: annotate function parameters and returns at minimum
Data shapes: `type SaveData = {...}` for DataStore payloads
Modules' public APIs — types are documentation the compiler enforces
whenNotToUse: Don't fight the system with `any` sprinkled everywhere to silence errors — fix the types or use targeted casts with comments
Legacy scripts: migrate gradually rather than boiling the ocean
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
--!strict

local function heal(target: Humanoid, amount: number)
    target.Health += amount
end

heal("hi", 5)    -- ✗ type error caught in the editor,
                 --   before the game ever runs
```
tips: Start modules with `--!strict` for the strongest checking
Define types for your data early — they ripple through autocomplete everywhere
`typeof(x)` in type positions infers from a value; handy for Instance subclasses
commonMistakes: Thinking annotations change runtime behavior — they don't; they're erased before execution
Confusing `type` (type declaration) with the `type()` value function
Using `::` casts to bypass real type errors instead of modeling the types correctly

examples.title: Typed save data
examples.code:
--!strict

export type SaveData = {
    coins: number,
    level: number,
    inventory: { string },
}

local function loadDefault(): SaveData
    return {
        coins = 0,
        level = 1,
        inventory = {},
    }
end

local data: SaveData = loadDefault()
data.coins += 10
-- data.coinss += 1   -- ✗ typo caught by the type checker
examples.whyItWorks: The SaveData alias describes the exact shape; any deviation — typos, missing fields, wrong types — becomes an editor error.
